title: Choose a, an or the
objective: Introduce one item, refer to it again, and write a general fact.

slides.title: Decide what the reader knows
body: For a first mention of one countable thing, use a or an. Use an before a vowel sound.
Use the when your reader can identify the thing. For plural nouns in general statements, often use no article.

slides.title: Follow one animal
body: “A frog sat on a leaf. The frog jumped into the pond.”
A introduces one frog. The points back to that frog.
“Frogs can jump.” This statement is about frogs in general.

slides.title: Read the first case together
body: First mention: ___ insect landed on a leaf. Later: ___ insect moved away. General fact: ___ insects have six legs.

slides.title: Try it with a partner
body: Fill the gap in the first sentence. Explain your choice.
Fill the gap in the second sentence. Explain your choice.

slides.title: Try a new case
body: First mention: ___ owl sat in a tree. Later: ___ owl flew away. General fact: ___ owls are birds.

slides.title: Work on your own
body: Fill the gap in the first sentence. Explain your choice.
Fill the gap in the second sentence. Explain your choice.
Write the general fact. Decide if the gap needs an article.

slides.title: Explain one choice
body: Tell your partner which noun is new, which one is known, and which noun describes a whole group.
